content: Data extrapolated from regional datasets or neighboring countries is used to estimate certain metrics. Estimates derived from a single program or region are included in the analysis. National estimates are provided, but their level of validation may vary. Validated national estimates are available for some parameters. Information on injection safety is either unavailable or derived from regional extrapolations or neighboring countries. Estimates from national surveys older than five years are included, but their relevance may be limited due to the age of the data. More recent estimates, derived from national surveys conducted within the last five years, are also included. Subnational-level data that has been validated is considered for certain metrics. Testing capacity for hepatitis B virus (HBV) is either not reported or based on extrapolated regional data, older surveys, or validated subnational data. For hepatitis C virus (HCV), there is either no information available or estimates are extrapolated from regional data, older surveys, or validated subnational data. Care and treatment data for HBV is either unavailable or derived from regional extrapolations, ad-hoc data sources, published studies, surveys, or patient registries. Similarly, care and treatment data for HCV is either unavailable or based on regional extrapolations, ad-hoc data sources, published studies, surveys, or patient registries. HBV refers to hepatitis B virus, HCV refers to hepatitis C virus, and HCC refers to hepatocellular carcinoma. This checklist does not establish minimum or gold standards but instead outlines a range of potential options for data collection and analysis. National stakeholders are responsible for determining the level of data quality that is both necessary and feasible within their specific national context.
